findings.where: Motion sketch section, the full-width panel behind it (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: The motion sketch sits on a large, saturated lavender field. That colour is not in the tile's own palette, which lists paper, grey, blue and pad yellow, and it is not one of the house colours. Below the hero it is the loudest block on the page. It breaks the quiet paper the whole direction promises and makes the sheet look like an unfinished demo panel.
findings.who_objects: The founder, who judges whether this direction is built in or around the house blue and grey. The brief makes those the only ink, and allows pale legal yellow only behind one quotation or the contact panel. A purple field contradicts the tile's own palette and texture notes ('flat and quiet'), and Mark would not see it as his look.

findings.where: Article specimen: the title 'The World's Best Public-Private Partnership Law', the subhead 'So, what are the key ‘chapter topics’?' and the 'Download' heading (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: The article's headings shout. The title is a heavy, bold serif, far from the light, refined line of the hero. The subhead and 'Download' are set in a wide, black grotesque that is neither of the tile's stated pair (Newsreader at 500 for subheads, Public Sans). On the article page these headings beat the text and the PDF link for attention. The type pair the tile shows above is not the one the article uses, so the specimen does not show the look holding up under real content.
findings.who_objects: The founder, who asked for 'refined, never childish' and serious type, and for the article specimen and PDF list as the product. A reader from a development bank would find a heavy display grotesque out of keeping with a legal advisor's writing. Angélique, adding headings later, would get type that does not match the advertised pair.

findings.where: Palette section, the four swatches (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: The four swatches are four different shapes. Paper is a square-cornered rectangle, grey is a rounded rectangle, blue is an ellipse and yellow has slight corners. They should read as one set of like things, but the mixed shapes break that, and the blue ellipse looks like a pill or a control more than a colour sample.
findings.who_objects: The founder reading the palette. They expect four comparable samples, and the shape change makes them wonder whether the blue or grey swatch means something different, such as a button shape the site will use.
